headline: Greater One-Horned Rhinos Reach 4,075 as Kaziranga Leads Conservation Win
meta_description: The global greater one-horned rhino population has climbed to 4,075, with Kaziranga in Assam driving this remarkable conservation success.
summary_short: The world's greater one-horned rhino population has reached 4,075, marking a significant recovery led by conservation efforts in Assam's Kaziranga.
body:
The global population of greater one-horned rhinos has climbed to 4,075, representing a major win for species recovery efforts worldwide.

Assam's Kaziranga has emerged as the epicenter of this revival, demonstrating what sustained conservation commitment can achieve. The sanctuary's success reflects decades of dedicated protection work that has transformed the fate of a species once hunted to the brink of extinction.

This growth signals hope not just for the greater one-horned rhino itself, but for landscape-scale conservation efforts across Asia. As these massive animals thrive again in their natural habitats, they serve as a reminder that recovery is possible when communities, governments, and conservationists work together toward a shared goal.
